key_insight: Scaling up GPT-style language models delays but does not eliminate plasticity loss, which still emerges during long training in both continual and stationary multilingual settings.
engineering_relevance: For continual-learning and long-running LLM systems, parameter scaling alone is not a sufficient safeguard; maintaining adaptivity will likely require training or optimization interventions beyond larger models.
method: Train GPT-style Transformer models from 5M to 314M non-embedding parameters on a multilingual continual-learning setup.
Track plasticity using a held-out Vietnamese probing task to detect deterioration in the ability to learn new information.
Compare continual-learning behavior with stationary multilingual training to test whether plasticity loss also appears without abrupt task switches.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent plasticity loss across all tested model sizes, with onset following a sublinear scaling law and measurable degradation on the Vietnamese probing task.
watch_item: The main evidence is based on one probing task and one multilingual setup, so the scaling trend may not generalize to all domains, architectures, or adaptation objectives.
paper_title: Can Scale Save Us From Plasticity Loss in Large Language Models?
